stories.title: SpiceJet fleet shrinks to six aircraft
stories.summary: SpiceJet is operating roughly 20 flights daily with a fleet reduced to six aircraft. Promoter Ajay Singh met with civil aviation officials to discuss the airline's status as it continues to face operational disruptions. The carrier currently serves a handful of routes across the country.

stories.title: SpiceJet passengers report widespread service issues
stories.summary: A LocalCircles survey found that every SpiceJet flier polled experienced timeliness issues over the past year. Nine in ten reported problems with customer service, while eight in ten cited issues with transparency. The airline is currently cancelling more than half of its daily flights.

stories.title: Regulator demands explanation from SpiceJet
stories.summary: The DGCA has issued a seven-day show-cause notice to SpiceJet regarding repeated operational disruptions and regulatory violations. The regulator cited concerns over declining on-time performance, frequent flight cancellations, and inadequate passenger facilitation. The airline must now explain its failure to operate according to its approved schedule.

stories.title: SpiceJet continues selling tickets for cancelled routes
stories.summary: SpiceJet is accepting bookings for flights it cannot operate, including routes to Dubai and Mumbai. The airline provides no disruption warnings to passengers, even as its fleet has dwindled to five active aircraft and the regulator investigates mounting cancellations and passenger hardship.

stories.title: Belgian strike to halt flights
stories.summary: Brussels Airport expects major disruptions on November 23 as air traffic controllers join a national demonstration. Skeyes stated it cannot provide normal services during the strike, forcing the cancellation of most arrivals and departures. The disruption is expected to last for 14 hours.

stories.title: No cancellation alerts, missing refunds: Uncertainty facing SpiceJet passengers as DGCA steps in - Moneycontrol.com
Navi Mumbai airport handles 27,000 passengers
stories.summary: Navi Mumbai International Airport recorded its busiest day since opening, managing 27,000 passengers and 212 aircraft movements on November 20. IndiGo accounted for the highest volume of traffic, operating 122 of the total movements. The facility handled a mix of scheduled, cargo, and general aviation flights.

stories.title: Free shuttle services end at Navi Mumbai airport
stories.summary: Travelers between Navi Mumbai and Mumbai airports must now pay for transport following the discontinuation of free shuttle services. Cityflo has exited the route, following the earlier withdrawal of Chalo Bus. Complimentary connectivity options along the corridor have now been fully removed.

stories.title: Gulf airlines protest Navi Mumbai slot dispute
stories.summary: Eleven Gulf carriers have petitioned the Civil Aviation Ministry after being denied historical flight slots at Mumbai International Airport. The airlines warn of potential diplomatic escalation if their existing access is not restored during the redevelopment of Terminal 1. The dispute remains unresolved.

stories.title: Air Canada reduces international route network
stories.summary: Air Canada has cut international flights by 19 percent compared to 2018 levels. While the airline is utilizing higher-capacity equipment to maintain seat counts, long-haul activity has declined. The carrier currently averages 265 daily international departures across its network.

stories.title: Allegiant Air removes 26 routes
stories.summary: Allegiant Air has cut 26 nonstop routes from its network when comparing the first quarter of 2026 to the same period in 2027. The leisure-focused carrier removed the links from both existing and discontinued airport locations as part of a schedule adjustment.

stories.title: WestJet ends Tulum service
stories.summary: WestJet will discontinue flights to Tulum, joining other carriers that have scaled back operations at the airport in favor of Cancun. The move leaves only two Canadian airlines serving the destination. The withdrawal is scheduled for January 9.

stories.title: Delta Air Lines to announce new long-haul route
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines plans to unveil a new nonstop route at an event in Seattle on December 2. The carrier has been expanding its transpacific network, recently reinstating services to Hong Kong and Tokyo. Industry expectations suggest the new destination may be Singapore.

stories.title: Lufthansa Group consolidates apps
stories.summary: The Lufthansa Group has launched a single mobile application to manage bookings and loyalty services across six of its airlines. The app appeared on the Apple App Store without prior announcement, centralizing functions previously handled by individual carrier platforms.

stories.title: Flydubai nears Tel Aviv flight resumption
stories.summary: Israel’s Ministry of Transportation has approved the resumption of flydubai flights to Tel Aviv. The decision follows a security review conducted two months after a first officer was accused of planning to crash a passenger jet. Final approval from security services is still pending.

stories.title: AirAsia reports narrowed quarterly losses
stories.summary: AirAsia Group reported a net loss for the third quarter that was half of the previous period's total. CEO Bo Lingam stated that the worst is behind the company, citing a sharp rise in operating earnings despite the typically slow monsoon season.

stories.title: Air Niugini flight diverts after fire warning
stories.summary: An Air Niugini Boeing 767 diverted to Davao, Philippines, after the crew received an engine fire indication while en route to Port Moresby. All 137 passengers and nine crew members landed safely. The crew shut down the affected engine at flight level 330.

Xiamen Airlines orders 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft
stories.summary: Xiamen Airlines has signed an agreement to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft for a list price of US$7.4 billion. Deliveries are scheduled from 2031 to 2034 as the carrier prepares for a move to a new hub. The airline will receive a bulk discount on the order.

stories.title: China's Xiamen Airlines Signs On For 50 Boeing 737 MAXs - Aviation Week
stories.summary: SINGAPORE,Xiamen Airlines has signed an agreement with Boeing for 50 737-8 aircraft, marking the largest Boeing order from China since 2017. The order comes six months after U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to Beijing in May, when he first alluded to a major order for U.S. passenger aircraft from... Already

stories.title: Xiamen Airlines Places $7.4 Billion Order For 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8s Ahead Of New Hub Move
stories.summary: Xiamen Airlines has placed an order for 50 brand-new Boeing 737 MAX 8 narrowbody twinjets. The deal was confirmed in a November 24 stock exchange filing by China Southern Airlines, its parent company. The aircraft, which will be delivered from 2031 to 2034, have a total list price of $7.4

Biman Bangladesh orders 10 Airbus aircraft
stories.summary: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has placed a firm order for 10 Airbus aircraft, including four A350-900 widebody jets and six A321neo single-aisle aircraft. The airline intends to use the new fleet to support its international network expansion to North America, Europe, and the Middle East.

stories.title: KLM shifts short-haul fleet strategy
stories.summary: KLM has cancelled plans to take delivery of the Airbus A320neo, opting instead to focus on Embraer E195-E2 aircraft to improve profitability. The A320neos previously allocated to the Dutch carrier will be transferred to Transactiva starting in 2028. The airline will retain its A321neo order.

stories.title: Chicago O'Hare flights delayed by radar outage
stories.summary: A runway surveillance system outage at Chicago O'Hare on November 24 forced the FAA to halt some flights. The disruption resulted in an average delay of 47 minutes, with some flights experiencing delays of up to 99 minutes. The system monitors aircraft and vehicles on runways.

New FAA Rule Takes Effect Ahead of Thanksgiving, Could Mean Longer Airport Delays - Men's Journal
FAA’s oversight of Boeing subject of new audit - The Seattle Times
FAA updates runway safety rules for holiday travel
stories.summary: The FAA is requiring a dedicated supervisor to be on duty before controllers can permit aircraft to line up and wait on runways. The agency implemented the change during the Thanksgiving travel week, stating that the new rule will not impact airport operations.

stories.title: Lawmakers Question FAA’s Nationwide AI Rollout
stories.summary: A group of 24 House Democrats sent a letter Tuesday questioning the FAA’s decision to expand its artificial intelligence-supported air traffic management system nationwide. Led by House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member Rick Larsen, D-Wash., the lawmakers requested documentation of the system’s safety validation ahead of its nationwide deployment

House Democrats question FAA's AI air traffic system
stories.summary: Two dozen House Democrats have requested validation data for the FAA's AI-supported airspace planning system, known as SMART. Lawmakers criticized the November 10 nationwide deployment, citing concerns that the platform was expanded without sufficient evidence of safety testing or safeguards against potential system outages.

stories.title: Nigeria plans regional aviation training hub in Abuja
stories.summary: Baze Aviation School is developing a flight training facility in Abuja with federal government support. Minister Festus Keyamo intends for the site to become a regional hub to reduce reliance on overseas training. Founder Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed reports the runway sub-base is nearly complete. Construction continues.

stories.title: Dayalans Aviation to open flight academy in Karnataka
stories.summary: Dayalans Aviation Private Limited has received approval to establish a flight training organisation at Hubballi Airport. The academy aims to launch by April or May 2027, subject to infrastructure and regulatory milestones. It will be the airport's second provider, adding capacity to northern Karnataka.

stories.title: Tassili Travail Aérien launches flight academy in Algeria
stories.summary: Tassili Travail Aérien has opened its flight academy at Sayada Airport, with training sessions scheduled to begin on 2 January 2027. The facility offers private, commercial, and airline transport pilot qualifications. Pre-registration for the inaugural intake is now open for prospective students.

stories.title: TAAG Angola Airlines opens local simulator facility
stories.summary: TAAG Angola Airlines has inaugurated a flight simulator facility at Luanda's new international airport. The centre houses two simulators intended for preliminary trainee assessments before students head overseas for further training. The Boeing 737 device is currently awaiting certification from the national aviation authority.

stories.title: Texas Southern University renews pilot training partnership with Southwest amid surge in enrollment - The Business Journ
Emirates honours top national cadets
stories.summary: Emirates held its first Recognition Day to celebrate the achievements of cadets within its National Cadet Pilot Programme. The event acknowledged the performance of UAE national cadets and the contributions of their instructors throughout the training journey.

stories.title: Phoenix approves police helicopter training contract
stories.summary: The Phoenix City Council has approved a five-year contract with Quantum Helicopters to train police pilots. The agreement, valued at up to $437,570, takes effect on 1 January 2027. The training is intended to ensure pilots maintain the skills required for law enforcement and public safety missions.

stories.title: Aeros Flight Training partners with IAGO for multi-crew instruction
stories.summary: Aeros Flight Training has named IAGO Flight Training as its recommended provider for airline-focused multi-crew cooperation courses. The partnership allows Aeros students to transition into A320 and 737 simulator instruction. Aeros has operated as a modular training organisation in the UK since 1986.

stories.title: Sinclair Community College tests electric aircraft training
stories.summary: Sinclair Community College and BETA Technologies conducted a demonstration flight of an electric aircraft in Ohio on 18 November. The event supports a partnership to integrate electric aircraft familiarisation and maintenance education into the college curriculum. The college currently offers various aviation technology programs.

research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A Viscosity-Decoupled Uzawa Lattice Boltzmann Method for Incompressible Flows Across Reynolds Numbers
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional lattice Boltzmann methods (LBMs) tie viscosity to collision relaxation, which induces diffusive stiffness at low Reynolds numbers, non-hydrodynamic instabilities at high Reynolds numbers, and passband breakdown in variable-relaxation dual-time schemes, whereas continuum incompressible solvers require. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Turbulence states vary widely in modeling difficulty, requiring distinct paradigms, thus, no single AI or data-driven approach suits all flows. We propose an operational framework classifying data-driven turbulence modeling by balancing physical causation and statistical correlation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Advanced Reactance Method - A Novel Approach for Distance Protection in Presence of Grid-Following Inverter-Based-Resources
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Renewable Energy Sources and consequently inverter-based resources (IBRs) are increasing worldwide. Grid-following (GFL) IBR control is the state-of-the-art. GFL IBRs exhibit different fault behavior compared to classical synchronous generators -- particularly in terms of Fault-Ride-Through (FRT). Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Algebraic Observability for Power System Dynamic State Estimation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing observability methods for dynamic state estimation are developed for ordinary differential equation (ODE) models, whereas power systems are naturally described by differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Applying these methods generally requires a DAE-to-ODE transformation, usually Kron reduction. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Implicit Discrete Adjoint Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Sensitivity Analysis and Shape Optimization in Multiscale Gas Flows
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and efficient gradient-based sensitivity evaluation remains challenging for performance optimization in multiscale flows with complex geometries. To address this challenge, this work develops a matrix-free discrete adjoint method for the steady implicit unified gas-kinetic scheme. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel model predictive control (MPC) formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment. The UAV is equipped with. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Collision of a sphere and a prolate spheroid settling in a quiescent ambient
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The collision rate of a prolate spheroid and a sphere settling through a quiescent fluid at small Reynolds number is computed for randomly oriented spheroids and for spheroids turned broadside by weak fluid inertia. Without hydrodynamic. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
